title: Hurricane Helene from the space station
description: External cameras on the International Space Station tracked Hurricane Helene across the Gulf of Mexico on Sept. 26, 2024. The station's robotic arm is visible on the right as the eye comes into view.
nasaTitle: Additional Views of Hurricane Helene from the International Space Station

title: Flying over Hurricane Idalia (Aug 29, 2023)
description: Part of a live view from the ISS as it passed over Hurricane Idalia before landfall in Florida. This cut picks up as the cloud tops fill the frame.
nasaTitle: HURRICANE IDALIA IS SEEN FROM THE INTERNATIONAL SPACE STATION

title: Hurricane Erin seen from orbit
description: Hurricane Erin photographed from the International Space Station on Aug. 19, 2025.
nasaTitle: Hurricane Erin Seen From International Space Station - 8-19-2025

title: STEVE: the purple ribbon that isn't an aurora
description: STEVE (Strong Thermal Emission Velocity Enhancement) is a thin ribbon of purple light first documented by aurora photographers. Ground photos and satellite data showed it behaves differently from a normal aurora.
nasaTitle: The Aurora Named STEVE

title: Seven years of the Sun in 2 minutes
description: Highlights from the Solar Dynamics Observatory's seventh year watching the Sun: flares, prominences and sunspots across several ultraviolet wavelengths.
nasaTitle: SDO: Year 7

title: The Moon crosses the Sun, then a flare erupts
description: On Jan. 30, 2014 the Moon passed between SDO and the Sun for two and a half hours, the longest lunar transit the observatory had recorded. A prominence eruption and an M-class flare followed.
nasaTitle: SDO Lunar Transit, Prominence Eruption, and M-Class Flare

title: Two weeks in the life of one sunspot
description: Active region 2665 rotates into view on July 5, 2017, grows, and rotates out of sight on July 17. Time-lapse from the Solar Dynamics Observatory.
nasaTitle: Two Weeks in the Life of a Sunspot

title: Three solar flares in 24 hours
description: Three mid-level flares erupted from the Sun on April 2–3, 2017. SDO captured all three.
nasaTitle: April 2017 Solar Flare Trio

title: A slow, looping eruption (April 2, 2014)
description: A mid-level flare peaked at 10:05 a.m. EDT on April 2, 2014. Flare radiation can't reach the ground, but strong flares can disturb the layer of the atmosphere used by GPS and radio.
nasaTitle: Graceful Eruption

title: An eruption arcs off the edge of the Sun
description: Over June 18, 2015 an eruption on the Sun's limb grew into a coronal mass ejection. Shown in 304 Å extreme ultraviolet light.
nasaTitle: Arching Eruption

title: Artemis II rolls out to Pad 39B (timelapse)
description: Crawler-transporter 2 carries the SLS rocket and Orion spacecraft on the 4.2-mile trip from the Vehicle Assembly Building to Launch Complex 39B on Jan. 17, 2026.
nasaTitle: Artemis II Rollout Timelapse

title: Full-duration SLS booster test fire
description: A full-scale solid rocket booster fires for a little over two minutes during a ground test in Promontory, Utah, on Sept. 2, 2020.
nasaId: NHQ_2020_0902_NASA CONDUCTS SPACE LAUNCH SYSTEM ROCKET FULL-SCALE BOOSTER TEST_FIX

title: Artemis I ascent from the rocket's own cameras
description: Cameras on the rocket recorded booster separation and jettison during the Artemis I ascent in November 2022.
nasaTitle: Artemis I Rocket Camera Footage of Ascent
source: http://images-assets.nasa.gov/video/Artemis I - Rocket Camera Footage/Artemis I - Rocket Camera Footage~small.mp4

title: Electron liftoff for NASA's PREFIRE mission
description: An Electron rocket lifts off from Māhia, New Zealand on May 25, 2024, carrying the first of two PREFIRE CubeSats that measure heat escaping from Earth's poles.
nasaTitle: Rocket Lab PREFIRE-1 Launch

title: Moving the SLS core stage onto a barge
description: The first SLS core stage leaves NASA's Michoud Assembly Facility in New Orleans and is rolled onto the Pegasus barge (Jan. 2020).
nasaTitle: NASA Rolls Out Space Launch System Rocket’s Core Stage from Michoud Factory

title: Perseverance landing, from the rover's cameras
description: Footage from Perseverance's entry, descent and landing cameras on Feb. 18, 2021: parachute deployment, heat shield separation, the surface of Jezero Crater, and touchdown.

title: How Webb was shaken before launch
description: At NASA Goddard, the James Webb Space Telescope was put on a shaker table to make sure it could survive the vibration of launch.
nasaTitle: Vibration Testing of NASA's James Webb Space Telescope

title: Webb in 30 seconds
description: A short look at what it took to build the James Webb Space Telescope.
nasaTitle: James Webb Space Telescope: Worth the Wait

title: Hubble at 29: the Southern Crab Nebula
description: Hubble marked 29 years in orbit with a new view of the Southern Crab Nebula, plus a few results from its 29th year.
nasaTitle: Hubble's 29th Anniversary

title: Releasing Hubble after its last servicing mission (animation)
description: Animation of the Hubble Space Telescope being released from the shuttle's robotic arm at the end of Servicing Mission 4.
nasaTitle: HST SM4 Hubble Deploy
